result.topic_en: Corollaries on residues of geometric progression powers modulo a prime 2n+1 when a^n leaves residue -1: residues of a^{n+λ} are complements of those of a^λ, and a scholium on paired residues symmetric about the middle residue -1.
result.transcription:
PER NVMEROS PRIMOS. 103

Coroll. 1.

41. Si ergo residua ex initio progreſſionis geometricae $1, a, a^2, a^3$ etc. nata ſint $1, \alpha, \beta, \gamma$ etc. reſidua ex terminis $a^n, a^{n+1}, a^{n+2}, a^{n+3}$ etc. nata erunt $-1, -\alpha, -\beta, -\gamma$ etc. ſeu $2n, 2n+1-\alpha, 2n+1-\beta, 2n+1-\gamma$ etc. cum ſit $\alpha = \alpha$, $\beta = a\alpha$, $\gamma = a\beta$ etc. ſemperque ſequens terminus oriatur ex praecedente per radicem $a$ multiplicato.

Coroll. 2.

42. Series ergo reſiduorum completa, cuius terminorum numerus eſt $= 2n$, antequam iidem termini recurrant, in duas partes diſpeſcitur $1, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ etc. et $-1, -\alpha, -\beta, -\gamma, -$ etc. cuius poſterioris termini ſunt complementa terminorum prioris; ſeu reſidua ex terminis $a^\lambda$ et $a^{n+\lambda}$ nata ſimul ſumta ſunt $= 0$ ſiue diuiſorem $2n+1$ praebent.

Scholion.

43. Quae de binis reſiduis ſociis ſuper ſunt obſeruata, quorum productum vnitate ſuperat multiplum diuiſoris, ea hic ita ſunt diſpoſita, vt a medio, quod eſt $-1$ vel $2n$ aequidiſtent. Si enim $r$ et $s$ ſint reſidua ex poteſtatibus $a^{n+\nu}$ et $a^{n-\nu}$ nata; productum $rs$ erit reſiduum ex poteſtate $a^{2n}$ natum, quod cum ſit vnitas, erit $rs = 1$ vel $1 + m(2n+1)$. Ipſum autem reſiduum medium $-1$ ſeu $2n$ ſibi ipſum eſt ſocium, omnino vti primum $+1$ ſe ipſum habet pro ſocio. Reliqua reſidua

items.quote: reſidua ex terminis $a^n, a^{n+1}, a^{n+2}, a^{n+3}$ etc. nata erunt $-1, -\alpha, -\beta, -\gamma$ etc.
items.english: The residues arising from the terms a^n, a^{n+1}, a^{n+2}, a^{n+3}, etc. will be -1, -α, -β, -γ, etc.

items.quote: reſidua ex terminis $a^\lambda$ et $a^{n+\lambda}$ nata ſimul ſumta ſunt $= 0$ ſiue diuiſorem $2n+1$ praebent.
items.english: The residues arising from the terms a^λ and a^{n+λ}, taken together, equal 0, i.e. give the divisor 2n+1.

items.quote: Si enim $r$ et $s$ ſint reſidua ex poteſtatibus $a^{n+\nu}$ et $a^{n-\nu}$ nata; productum $rs$ erit reſiduum ex poteſtate $a^{2n}$ natum, quod cum ſit vnitas, erit $rs = 1$ vel $1 + m(2n+1)$.
items.english: For if r and s are the residues arising from the powers a^{n+ν} and a^{n-ν}, the product rs will be the residue arising from the power a^{2n}, which, since it is unity, gives rs = 1 or 1 + m(2n+1).
